statements.round1:
Title: Calibrated Reasoning in Fictional Multi-Agent Systems
Keywords: calibration, agents
Abstract: This entirely synthetic paper proposes a calibration method and evaluates it on controlled simulated tasks.

statements.round2:
Reviewer 1: The method is clear and the controlled results support the stated claims.
Reviewer 2: The ablations are useful; the limitations should be made more prominent.

statements.round3: Author response: We will expand the limitations and clarify that the experiments use only synthetic environments.

statements.round1:
Title: An Imaginary Benchmark Without Baselines
Keywords: benchmark, evaluation
Abstract: This synthetic submission introduces a small benchmark but reports no comparison systems or validation.

statements.round2:
Reviewer 1: The motivation is relevant, but there are no baselines and the sample is too small.
Reviewer 2: The evaluation does not establish reliability or novelty.

statements.round3: Author response: We acknowledge that baseline experiments and validation are not yet available.

statements.round1:
Title: Robust Graph Inference on Constructed Worlds
Keywords: graphs, robustness
Abstract: This fictional study provides a reproducible graph suite and a simple robust inference algorithm.

statements.round2:
Reviewer 1: The release is reproducible and the analysis is careful.
Reviewer 2: Gains are modest but consistent across the declared settings.

statements.round3: Author response: We added confidence intervals and clarified the narrow scope of the conclusions.
